tools.description: Shadow mode for the Nx cut-over: runs the current planner and nx affected for one change, maps Nx tasks onto CI lanes and reports where they disagree. Run by the non-gating nx-shadow workflow; deleted with the planner.
Nx chooses which CI lanes run for pull requests and queue groups. The planner's selection stands for main, nightly and full runs, and whenever Nx cannot answer.
Nx plugin that turns every pubspec.yaml and independently locked npm package into an Nx project, adds path and declared cross-language edges, and gives source projects a generator check target.
Validates the tool manifest, lists and dispatches registered commands, and fail-closed selects checks from explicit or affected paths without creating a second execution-authority layer.

Chooses the strict Firestore/Storage emulator tests a pull request can reach, from the dependency-cruiser graph of functions/ plus the data files tests name; shared inputs and rules changes keep the full list, and only pull requests narrow.

Derives which active tools reach each repository file through static imports, using the pinned dependency-cruiser in tool/impact, so affected-tool selection owns code inputs without hand-written globs.

Validates the tool manifest: ids, paths and CI requirements, each tool's role, that a gate or ratchet has a check that executes it, that an internal gate's node tests run under an active tool, and that every rule sits complete on one active tool.
Classifies exact four-tree merge outcomes and requires reasoned receipts for every discarded side in strict mode.

Validates source-owned Markdown identity, version, date, owner, and lifecycle metadata; rejects duplicate identities, semantic version decreases, and identity swaps while reporting reviewed deletions without a duplicate catalog.

rules.title: Prefer versioned owners over new markdown sprawl
rules.instruction: Update an existing source-of-truth document before creating a new one. Mark stale snapshots historical or delete them after their durable content moves. Markdown frontmatter is the document's metadata authority; do not update a parallel version catalog.

tools.description: Plans fail-closed CI, release, and deploy impact from the source-owned component graph and runs only explicitly allowlisted compile-codegen checks.
checks: node --test tool/harness/lib/git_changes.test.mjs tool/harness/lib/flutter_document_selection.test.mjs tool/lib/path_glob.test.mjs tool/harness/component_graph.test.mjs tool/harness/check_flutter_l10n_generated.test.mjs tool/harness/harness_cli.test.mjs tool/harness/workflow_wiring.test.mjs

rules.title: Use read-only impact planning for broad AI-assisted work
rules.instruction: For broad work, inspect the Git diff and use the read-only Catch planner to explain affected components and checks. Run the selected checks and preserve proof in Git and CI. Do not write registry receipts, readiness metrics, or regression ledgers.

tools.description: Derives the locally runnable CI gates for a change from the workflow definitions themselves, so pre-push verification cannot drift from what CI actually runs.

Thin ordinary-Git task safety: exact bases, disjoint claims, protected handoff/abandonment, and dry-run guarded retirement with accepted-source equivalence, preserved recovery, manual owner clearance and non-forced worktree removal. Never installs, validates, pushes, deletes refs or authorizes cleanup.

rules.title: Keep parallel agent work parent-integrated and worktree-isolated
rules.instruction: Use an exact-base Git worktree for parallel tasks, declare disjoint claimed paths, reject overlap with active local tasks, review commits before integration, refuse ordinary handoff while unique work is uncommitted or unpushed, and run final verification in the integration branch. Reject stale launcher lifecycle files; plain finish must not release a claim. Explicit retained handoff preserves the original claim and states its next action. Keep the task claim through acceptance, then use the existing dry-run retire and normally admitted non-forced apply path. Prove accepted-source equivalence and exact recovery, preserve dirty/untracked/ignored files and active ownership, and report retirement or its exact accountable retention reason and next action. External acceptance, cross-clone ownership/runtime clearance and deletion authority are named manual completion checks. A deliberately superseded claim may be abandoned only from a clean worktree with an attributable local reason record. Keep coordination state local and disposable; do not write delegation metrics or tracked receipts.

tools.description: Bootstraps a fresh Git worktree with only its selected isolated root npm, Functions npm, or Flutter dependencies from committed lockfiles; defaults to all three.
Keeps staged Dart formatting and every catalogued committed compile-codegen output synchronized without running broad analysis.

rules.title: Keep committed generated artifacts synchronized before review
rules.instruction: Install the repository-local pre-commit hook. Regenerate localization inputs, format staged Dart without absorbing partial work, and run the source-owned freshness check for every triggered committed compile-codegen output before review. The schema contract outputs aren't committed: the hook regenerates them when their inputs are staged, and stages nothing.

tools.description: Classifies remote or local branches using ancestry, exact tree history, exact merged-PR identity, final changed-path identity, age, and open-PR state so completed refs can be pruned without hiding abandoned code.

rules.title: Keep completed branches disposable and surface abandoned code
rules.instruction: Delete single-use branches after semantic integration is proven. Audit remote refs daily, never auto-delete open-PR or unique-looking work, and fail visibly when a branch remains outside main without an open PR beyond the review window.

tools.description: Creates and verifies ephemeral exact-SHA, source-run, and SHA-256 artifact provenance plus ordered idempotent deployment checkpoints for CI/CD promotion and resume.
Reads exact Firebase Hosting custom-domain readiness and provisions only a missing resource with a current binding guard.
Reconciles exact custom form origins across Auth, App Check Enterprise keys and upload CORS while preserving unrelated grants.
Plans and explicitly applies client form-domain onboarding and rollback with exact project, reservation and manager authority.
Selects the authorized Functions affected by exact committed module dependencies and the npm packages they load, with full snapshot and conservative fallback behavior.
Tests per-export runtime dependency fingerprints with conservative unknown-impact rejection; promotion integration requires independent source and immutable package evidence.
Verifies the fixed preview-only measurement runtime, accepted main CI, exact static bytes and serving privacy headers; production tracking remains disabled.

Fails when any staged Functions TypeScript module, including a test helper, has an unresolved relative import; reads exact index blobs so untracked working-tree files cannot mask an omitted source dependency.
Keeps Firestore validation failures visible while explicitly saving the complete diagnostic report for upload.

Projects one production Admin, Host Flutter web, or Marketing Hosting bundle into a bounded lifecycle-hook-free Firebase package for the exact Catch production project and surface site, with exact workflow/run/source binding and a strict per-file digest inventory.
Evaluates sanitized expected and observed source/run evidence at the final website-promotion freshness gate and refuses any mismatch after at most one no-cache reread.

Guards the exact Admin, standalone Host, and Marketing Hosting path: runtime-complete triggers, one production build, immutable artifact-id and digest promotion, no deploy-time rebuild, current-main freshness, and terminal source-bound recovery.

Discovers every tracked or untracked Dart and Flutter pubspec, resolves standalone packages plus the root workspace, and requires zero analyzer diagnostics across the root app, Consumer, Host, Widgetbook, and nested tooling packages.
Polls project-bound Firestore composite-index metadata until every desired packaged index is READY, failing closed on terminal states or timeout before dependent backend stages continue.

Normalizes only the verified Firebase deploy copy: removes obsolete collection-scoped non-vector one-field declarations after retirement and field-override checks, and removes repeated identical complete index definitions while preserving their first occurrence.

Materializes validated non-secret Firebase Functions parameters only inside the disposable deploy tree, preserving fail-closed WhatsApp provider state for legacy packages while allowing non-interactive parameter discovery.
Parses non-secret Functions parameter declarations without executing source and rejects gaps in the deploy materializer or the exact deployment dotenv file before mutation.

Prints optional read-only guidance from the current Git SHA and source-owned scope, skills, rules, owner docs, and locally safe checks. It grants no execution or write authority and stores no receipt.
Regression-checks canonical Flutter app-target arguments and narrowly bounded CI-only retries for verified CocoaPods Git TLS and Gradle-wrapper download failures.
Scans backend error handling migration candidates.

rules.title: Keep the app error catalogue current
rules.instruction: When adding, renaming, or removing an AppException subclass, stable error code, error mapper, AppErrorContext, branded error primitive, or repeated app-facing failure category, update the error handling contract and error quick-reference sections in docs/app_architecture.md in the same pass. Add typed exceptions only for stable product/domain errors that need branching, analytics, retry policy, or tests; use mapped copy for one-off message changes.

tools.description: Scans frontend, provider, plugin, and local error-handling migration candidates.

rules.title: Put plugin and platform side effects behind seams
rules.instruction: Store launches, URL launches, share sheets, image pickers, connectivity subscriptions, FCM setup, and other platform/plugin effects should sit behind providers/controllers/services so tests can replace them.

rules.title: Keep architecture exhibits fresh against the code they quote
rules.instruction: Every architecture reference exhibit must declare an exhibit-freshness marker naming the exhibit and its owner, and remove stale code snippets when the reference implementation changes.

tools.description: Checks app architecture reference exhibits for freshness markers and stale code snippets.

Checks what one file cannot show: tool/architecture/context_map.json is well formed and the architecture spec's context table matches it. Placement and import order are catch_arch_* lints that read the same map.

Moves legacy domain/ and data/ files into lib/contexts/<context>/ as tool/architecture/context_map.json places them, rewrites every Dart directive and whole-path mention, writes each context's public API file, and proves a move commit is mechanical (--verify). --imports-only updates another branch after the move lands.

Creates the files a new context package, screen, catch_ui component or web-ui component starts from, in the shape docs/app_architecture.md (App Roots) fixes. Prints what it cannot edit: workspace and dependency lines, the route and capture ids, the registry record and the web barrel lines. Refuses to overwrite.

Renames the club names the contracts declare (fields, enum values, collections, titles) across contracts, TypeScript, rules, indexes, fixtures and Dart strings, and TypeScript identifiers and file names. A club field beside its organizer twin collapses into the twin. The club subtype, BigQuery columns, copy and URLs stay. --verify proves a rename commit is exactly the codemod's output for its parent.

Renames Club to Organizer in Flutter code: Dart file and folder names, identifiers, code references in comments, localization keys, and the registries and tools that name them. Names the generated schema contracts declare, string literals and the club subtype stay. --verify proves a rename commit is exactly the codemod's output for its parent.
Checks production Dart build methods that read Mutation isPending state also expose mutation error feedback.

rules.title: A watched Mutation consumed for isPending must also surface hasError
rules.instruction: Any UI that watches a Mutation to drive a spinner (isPending) must also handle hasError — via an inline ErrorBanner.fromError, a screen-level listenToCatchMutationErrors, or try/catch + showCatchNoticeError around .run(). Silent failure (spinner clears, no feedback) is forbidden, especially for destructive/security actions.

tools.description: Enforces corrected Host CRM ownership, application routing, provenance, consent, communication-plan, saved-audience, manual-handoff, and count-copy boundaries.

rules.title: Keep Host CRM identity, provenance, permission, intent, route, and delivery authorities separate
rules.instruction: Keep contact identity, immutable provenance, participant-controlled communication permission, organizer suppression, host intent, server-resolved route, manual work, and provider delivery evidence as separate authorities. Audience owns People, saved audiences, Forms, Applications, and Responses; the Forms domain retains response/application semantics and mutation ownership without becoming a global shell destination. Inbox consumes audience references and owns Sends/Inbox composition. Legacy Customers and Forms application links redirect to Audience. Host Forms may append source-backed contact provenance or prepare reviewed work but ordinary form consent never grants marketing permission and automations never dispatch outreach. External handoff may record only device acceptance and explicit host assertions, never delivery or read state. Visible Host CRM counts use ICU plural ownership.

tools.description: Checks production Dart navigation calls outside lib/routing avoid raw route path string literals.

rules.title: Navigation outside routing config uses named routes or constants
rules.instruction: Production navigation outside lib/routing must use named routes, route constants, or typed route helpers instead of raw path string literals. Raw paths stay owned by route definitions and URL contract files.

tools.description: Fails on any live widget/design-system cleanup candidate.
Validates the consolidated remote operations inventory.
Checks React admin app, feature, shared, and generated import boundaries.
Checks the live website/admin/web-ui TypeScript dependency topology, unresolved local imports, direct cross-surface boundaries, and runtime cycles; deterministic JSON evidence is emitted on demand.

rules.title: Keep React dependency topology deterministic and surface-safe
rules.instruction: Check the React dependency graph live from current TypeScript sources. Repo-local imports must resolve, website and admin may share through governed packages rather than importing each other directly, and runtime dependencies must be acyclic without an allowlist. Type-only cycles remain visible without blocking the check. Keep summary and JSON evidence available for unhealthy graphs; do not commit generated graph projections. Run node tool/web/react_dependency_graph.mjs --check whenever React imports or workspace exports move.

tools.description: Fails on user-visible marketing website strings outside website/src/content and the reasoned allowlist.

rules.title: Keep marketing-authored website copy in the content layer
rules.instruction: User-visible marketing-authored strings belong under website/src/content, in page-specific content modules. Permanent technical exceptions require an exact-string allowlist entry with a reason.

tools.description: Validates typed Flutter ARB copy metadata, rejects generated visibleCopy-style identifier keys unless explicitly allowlisted, and can export a marketing review CSV.

rules.title: Product copy is owned by typed, reviewable locale catalogs
rules.instruction: Handwritten user-facing Flutter copy belongs in packages/l10n/lib/app_en.arb with description, audience, owner, and surface metadata and is consumed through generated AppLocalizations. Domain and controller layers carry semantic ids, codes, and placeholder data rather than localized prose. Native permission copy belongs in copy/native_en.json and notification templates belong in copy/notifications_en.json; generated consumers must stay in sync. Inline technical identifiers, test fixtures, and user-authored content require narrow documented exemptions rather than broad folders.

tools.description: Blocks unmanaged Flutter product copy in widget arguments, copy-shaped defaults and initializers, presentation-state members, validator/share/status helpers, and Event Success display enums; the checked baseline must remain empty.
Derives exact handwritten Flutter localization-key usage live and fails on missing catalog getters or any zero-use catalog key; complete JSON evidence is ephemeral.
Runs seeded metadata validation probes for the Flutter ARB copy catalog.
Migrates eligible user-visible literals from clean Flutter files into the typed ARB catalog while preserving copy whitespace.
Validates marketing-owned Event Success questionnaire copy and keeps the typed Dart domain catalog generated from locale JSON.
Validates marketing-owned structured domain copy and regenerates typed Event Success and event-policy catalogs from Dart structure templates.
Keeps iOS permission copy generated from the marketing-reviewable native English catalog.
Keeps Functions notification templates generated from the marketing-reviewable English catalog.
Checks React marketing website app, content, feature, shared, generated, and service import boundaries.
Enforces the shared ESLint UI preset and exact shrink-only app suppressions; replaces the raw-control and class-name scanners.

rules.title: React interactive UI must use shared primitives
rules.instruction: React production UI composes library components instead of raw markup or className/style overrides. The shared ESLint preset records existing production debt in each app eslint-suppressions.json; counts must match source and may never grow above accepted main. Table/image families wait for their styled components (D17). Story/test control and class-name ownership guards remain in the preset. Run node tool/run.mjs check web:react-ui-lint before handoff.

tools.description: Checks React website/admin feature code routes governed component families through shared primitives, and verifies adopted admin form families declare valid shared field-row interaction modes directly from current source and authored component contracts.

rules.title: React governed component families must use shared wrappers
rules.instruction: React feature, app, and story code must route governed component families through shared primitives instead of rendering the shell directly. Marketing website exported uppercase feature components must be declared in design/website/components.json or made private, so route/section/supporting components remain registry-backed. Admin feature UI files may export route/workspace entry components such as *Screen and *Workspace; reusable panels, cards, lists, badges, and sections belong in admin/src/shared/ui or stay private. Admin route/workspace entries, shared admin primitives, and admin feedback providers must be declared in design/admin/components.json. Every exported React component in website, admin and @catch/web-ui maps to a registry concept, a T4 owner or deletion in the generated inventory (web:shared-ui-adoption; --write saves build/react_component_inventory.json); a shared-layer export that matches a registered contract by name or renders its @catch/web-ui implementation records componentId, or comparedWith with a comparisonReason, in its surface registry. Production drawing belongs in @catch/web-ui. The shared ESLint preset ratchets raw elements and className/style props against existing app suppressions; do not add inline allow markers or grow recorded debt. The scanner owns its governed families in source and emits a current view with `node tool/web/check_react_component_governance.mjs --families-json`; do not check in a duplicate generated registry. The family scanner is a known-family blocklist: passing it does not classify novel component shells, so repeated new shell drift must become a scanner family before handoff. Run `node tool/run.mjs check marketing:website-components`, `node tool/run.mjs check web:admin-feature-exports`, `node tool/run.mjs check web:admin-components`, `node tool/run.mjs check web:react-ui-lint`, `node tool/run.mjs check web:react-component-governance`, and `node tool/run.mjs check web:shared-ui-adoption` before handoff.

tools.description: Checks admin feature UI only exports route/workspace entry components; reusable panels/cards/lists must live in shared admin primitives or stay private.

rules.title: Protect the submitted request snapshot while an operation is pending
rules.instruction: Every pending user operation must declare one integrity policy. Frozen snapshots disable request-defining inputs, conflicting actions, mutation-reset callbacks, and unsafe route exits until settlement. Versioned snapshots require immutable generations plus stale-result rejection or cancellation and tests. Independently keyed concurrency requires distinct typed scope keys and separate pending/error surfaces. A loading button alone is not sufficient; controllers must also deduplicate duplicate dispatches or use an equivalent idempotency boundary.

tools.description: Enforces one exclusive Admin operation lease across the controllers it names, the shared workspace/navigation boundary, and immutable-snapshot regression proof.

Requires every Admin navigation and Intake workspace to declare callable-backed live reads, rejects retained operational JSON snapshots and generated operational imports, and can verify every declared callable against a deployed Firebase environment.
Validates design/admin/components/ against admin route/workspace exports, shared admin UI primitives, feedback providers, and ready Storybook catchComponent coverage.
Checks React website/admin feature boundaries for route-owned state and cross-feature ownership drift.

rules.title: React server-state pending state must ratchet toward TanStack Query
rules.instruction: React feature controllers and feature use* hooks should not add new manual loading, saving, submitting, pending, or in-flight state for server reads or mutations. Use TanStack Query query/mutation state and explicit query-key invalidation for server state; keep only view-local form, filter, selection, and client-only rendering state in React state. Run node tool/run.mjs check web:react-query-state before handoff.

tools.description: Fails on React feature controller and use-hook manual async/loading state so new server-state work moves to TanStack Query instead of local loading flags.
Generates Catch app icon and splash PNG assets using AppKit and the bundled Archivo font; checks parse syntax only.

Generates flavor-specific native launcher and splash brand assets from the design context token cache, including Consumer responsive iOS launch geometry and Host-specific Archivo icon and centered splash assets.
Verifies Riverpod's analysis_server_plugin diagnostics are active in dart analyze.
Checks per-file lint fixture assertions and analyzer output attribution, refusing plugin crashes, malformed output, missing fixtures, and diagnostics from the wrong file.

Finds balanced Dart call blocks for the capture, route and Widgetbook checks, skipping line and block comments and plain, raw and triple-quoted strings so delimiters inside them never unbalance a block.
Verifies all Catch UI violation and clean-allowance fixtures with one analyzer invocation and independent per-file assertions.

rules.title: Codify audited UI invariants as analyzer plugin rules
rules.instruction: When a UI surface invariant is deterministic, move it into packages/catch_ui_lints as an analysis_server_plugin diagnostic that runs across handwritten lib/** by default. Verify Catch diagnostics with the seeded harness or repository-root dart analyze, never flutter analyze or a targeted subdirectory analysis. Generate steering tables from component contracts, use the resolved checker for cross-file composition, exempt only semantic source-of-truth folders or generated code, and keep broad scanners only for triage and migration discovery.

rules.title: Async loading states render credible data before blocking skeletons and always recover
rules.instruction: When credible initial or fallback data is available (route extra, cached value, optimistic snapshot), render it ahead of blocking loading states. Known layouts use CatchSkeleton.content or the matching CatchSection loading constructor and real CatchFieldLayout. When fetched data determines the page structure, preserve its known chrome and center progress in CatchStateViewport.loading or .sliverLoading; unresolved sheet and inline sections use a bounded CatchLoadingIndicator. Initial provider loads must reach an actionable error state after the shared presentation deadline, and CatchAsyncBoundary and its sliver constructor call sites must supply onRetry that restarts the failing provider boundary.

rules.title: Data-load errors must use a Catch primitive and blocking states must expose recovery
rules.instruction: AsyncValue/stream error branches must render CatchLocalizedErrorState (including inline/compact modes) or CatchLocalizedSliverErrorState with mapped copy. Provider failures use onRetry that invalidates the failing provider; terminal full-screen and sliver route errors use a truthful secondary action such as CatchErrorBackButton. Reserve CatchEmptyState for genuinely-empty success states; never route an error into an empty-state or a hand-rolled card that discards the error object.

rules.title: Network images go through a shared caching/decode-sized primitive
rules.instruction: Remote images must render through a shared CatchNetworkImage primitive providing caching, cacheWidth/cacheHeight decode sizing, a branded errorBuilder, and a loading placeholder. Raw Image.network in feature code is forbidden.

rules.title: Code lives in a declared bounded context and depends only downward
rules.instruction: Every handwritten lib Dart file is placed by tool/architecture/context_map.json in one of the declared bounded contexts or in the kernel, platform, pages or app layer. Layers import only downward (kernel, platform, contexts, pages, app), and a context imports only contexts declared before it. Code under lib/contexts/ crosses into another context only through that context's public API file lib/contexts/<name>/<name>.dart. A new top-level folder must be declared in the map before it holds code. When a screen needs two contexts, its view model combines them; one context never learns about another to save a screen work. These are catch_arch_* analyzer lints that read the map; audit:context-map keeps what one file cannot show, that the map is well formed and the spec's context table matches it. Files under the target roots take no exceptions. Since the phase 3 move, domain and data code lives under lib/contexts/ and a legacy feature folder keeps only its screens and barrel; any other file there fails catch_arch_legacy_context_file.

rules.title: Keep product behavior out of presentation widgets
rules.instruction: Widgets may own focus, scroll, animations, navigation, temporary input state, and rendering. Move repository writes, repository-provider reads, validation decisions, mutation orchestration, product side effects, and WidgetRef-threaded provider access into controllers, view-model providers, or repositories. Business loaded data, cursors, pending/error/retry and completion identity remain controller responsibilities even when an injected callback or generated action performs the write. Consumer widgets and controller filenames do not exempt these responsibilities. Keep genuine mechanical feedback distinct; preserve domain currentness, cancellation, snapshot and idempotency fences when moving ownership.

rules.title: Layer imports follow dependency direction
rules.instruction: Layer imports follow the declared dependency direction. lib/*/domain/** must not import Flutter, Riverpod, Firebase, routing, or platform plugin packages; Timestamp/serialization handling routes through core/firestore_converters, and new domain code must not add direct imports. lib/*/data/** and lib/*/domain/** must not import feature presentation code. Feature presentation must not import sibling feature presentation internals. Sanctioned seams are (a) a sibling feature public controller (presentation/*_controller.dart) imported from a route screen (*_screen.dart) or another controller, and (b) symbols exported by the sibling feature root barrel (lib/<feature>/<feature>.dart), where every presentation export in a barrel requires a // public-api: annotation. Direct deep imports of sibling presentation files remain violations. Widgets, bodies, state adapters, and view models are feature internals — when another feature needs a read model, expose a narrow public provider/contract or annotated barrel seam instead. The same rules apply by placement to the bounded-context roots: lib/contexts/<context>/domain/** and packages/kernel/** are domain, lib/contexts/<context>/data/** is data, actions/ are controllers, parts/ stay provider-free, and lib/pages/** and apps/<app>/lib/<destination>/** are screens; findings under these roots take no exceptions. These are catch_arch_* analyzer lints; an exception elsewhere is a // ignore: catch_ui_lints/<code> -- <reason> next to the code, which the lints reject when it is file-wide, unreasoned or stale. A provider-free file (a *_state.dart adapter, a context parts/ widget, or a file marked // architecture: provider-free) uses no Riverpod, routing, data-layer or repository API.

rules.title: Time-dependent domain getters take an injected clock, not DateTime.now()
rules.instruction: Domain getters/predicates with time semantics must accept an injected DateTime/referenceNow when any caller threads one, instead of calling DateTime.now() internally — otherwise adjacent branches disagree and tests cannot pin time.

rules.title: Do not idle-timeout realtime Firestore listeners
rules.instruction: Do not wrap Firestore snapshot streams in Stream.timeout to detect stalled loads; realtime streams may legitimately stay silent after initial data. Prefer Riverpod autoDispose, screen-active gating, explicit refresh/retry UI, and focused tests that advance fake time past prior timeout thresholds. Every keepAlive provider must carry a // keepalive: rationale marker within the three lines above the annotation or declaration.

tools.description: Projects focused Catch UI analyzer reports and rejects every Catch diagnostic at the aggregate zero gate.

rules.title: Keep design-system ownership centralized
rules.instruction: L0 generated scales, semantic roles, and component tokens live in packages/catch_tokens, whose only production dependency is Flutter. Shared foundations and branded font assets live under packages/catch_ui; its production dependencies are limited to Flutter, catch_tokens and Skeletonizer 2.1.3; icon glyphs come from the vendored font behind the icon role catalog. AppTheme only attaches the app activity palette to CatchTheme. Do not add new design primitives under generic lib/constants or a parallel top-level lib/theme folder.

rules.title: Avoid hardcoded widget dimensions for content-sized UI
rules.instruction: Treat fixed heights and widths on content-bearing widgets as a layout smell. Prefer intrinsic content sizing, flexible constraints, aspect ratios for truly fixed-format media, and min/max constraints only when they preserve responsiveness across screen sizes, text scale, localization, and variable backend content. Fixed dimensions are acceptable for icons, avatars, progress indicators, toolbars, known-format controls, and intentionally bounded visual assets, but cards, tiles, list rows, and sections should not depend on magic-number heights to look correct.

tools.description: Requires every active tool-manifest category to be scheduled by Tools CI and rejects unknown workflow categories.
Generates analyzer steering tables, contract expectations, and seeded steering probes from the component registry.
Requires every component to have static enforcement, executable contract verification, or an exceptional unexpired waiver, and every plugin/checker code to have a catalog owner.

Uses analyzer resolution to require branch-universal typed layout ownership for every statically reachable terminal of each rendered GoRoute and full-screen PageRoute presentation, fails unsupported PageRoute aliases, factories, tear-offs, builders, and subclasses closed, and reserves Flutter Scaffold construction, aliases, and subclasses for the canonical screen scaffold. Only direct MaterialPageRoute construction is supported by the generated imperative route inventory.
Checks that consumer and host form descriptors bind to generated schema field constraints, including a seeded contradictory-limit probe.

rules.title: Editable form constraints derive from schema contracts
rules.instruction: Every editable canonical control and form-descriptor instance in the Consumer and Catch Host apps must bind generated CatchContractFieldConstraints instead of repeating length, required, pattern, collection, enum, format, or numeric constraints. Typed choices must declare their wire-value serializer, range controls must bind both endpoints, and genuinely non-editable disclosures must carry an explicit audited exemption.

tools.description: Scans every editable canonical Flutter form control and descriptor instance directly from both installable apps, rejecting missing generated contracts, serializers, endpoint bindings, or explicit exemptions; an explicit non-check run writes only an ignored build report.
Runs the full data/schema/rules contract gate.
Runs all deterministic headless app-shell suites or a bounded native smoke/all scope on an explicitly selected Flutter device.
Turns Flutter LCOV into a visibility-only handwritten-code and feature-level report without imposing an aggregate percentage threshold.
Keeps Flutter test specs within 1,200 lines unless the spec states a reason in a size-exemption comment near its top; no spec may pass 2,500 lines. No baseline file.

rules.title: Keep Flutter test specs bounded while coverage remains honest evidence
rules.instruction: Keep Flutter test specs at or below 1,200 lines; a larger spec states its reason in a `// size-exemption: <reason>` comment in its first 20 lines, and no spec passes 2,500 lines. Use feature-level LCOV as visibility rather than an unsupported aggregate percentage threshold.

tools.description: Keeps handwritten Dart sources within 800 lines unless the file states a reason in a size-exemption comment near its top; no file may pass 2,500 lines. No baseline file; lib/routing/go_router.dart and the CatchField facade carry their reasons in the file.

rules.title: Bound handwritten Dart sources; exceptions state their reason in the file
rules.instruction: Keep handwritten Dart files at or below 800 lines. A larger file states its reason in a `// size-exemption: <reason>` comment in its first 20 lines, and no file passes 2,500 lines. Generated producer outputs are excluded by identity.

tools.description: Generates shared Flutter and Functions business constants.
Generates isolated Functions schemas, validators and catalogs plus test/tool inventories, paths and cross-runtime contracts.
Validates JSON schema source consistency.
Validates every contract fixture against its explicitly mapped generated JSON Schema.

rules.title: Contract fixtures stay schema-backed
rules.instruction: Every JSON fixture under contracts/fixtures/valid or contracts/fixtures/invalid must be declared in tool/contracts/check_schema_fixtures.mjs and must validate with the expected pass/fail result against its generated JSON Schema.

tools.description: Validates staged migration contract phase metadata and live-apply evidence.

rules.title: Migration contracts keep phase evidence machine-checkable
rules.instruction: Every migration contract must declare schemaVersion, logicalName, currentPhase, reason, unique phases with known statuses, operational evidence such as guards or known consumers, and liveApply evidence when any phase is complete_remote.

tools.description: Checks Firestore contract metadata against rules, schemas, and Functions exports.

Checks repository-owned composite Firestore query contracts against firestore.indexes.json, rejects uncontracted composite query builders, and blocks duplicate composite definitions and non-deployable single-field plus __name__ pseudo-composites.

rules.title: Composite Firestore queries stay synchronized with deployable index configuration
rules.instruction: Every repository-owned composite query builder declares its ordered firestore-index contract beside the query. The checked index configuration must contain every declared contract, retired collection indexes must not survive renames, duplicate composite definitions and non-deployable single-field plus __name__ pseudo-composites must be rejected, and the parity gate must run before deploy.

tools.description: Rejects numeric repository read limits and unbounded Firestore collection reads outside the canonical ReadLimitPolicy and reviewed-exception contracts.

rules.title: Repository read limits use one reviewed surface policy

Builds the Storybook workbench for route-linked marketing website component and page-state review.
Builds the Storybook workbench for registry-linked admin shared primitives and future admin route/workspace review states.

rules.title: Keep public viewer and listing authority behavior explicit across app and web
rules.instruction: Treat design/public_surface_behavior.json as the executable decision table for public app and marketing surfaces. Keep viewer-session resolution, app role, profile readiness, viewer relationship, app and web publication, organizer ownership/claim/verification, host/contact identity, event supply/lifecycle/availability/payment, location, independent claim/review capabilities, and their runtimes explicit. Every consumer route must have exactly one matrix owner, every configuration must be verified by the declared app or website harness, and excluded dimension values require a rationale. Public actions fail closed when relationship or runtime authority is unresolved.

Provides deterministic component-concept identity, collision-key, topology, and metric helpers.

Generates the redesign programme's component matrix from the registry and the two frameworks' public barrels: what exists today and what is left to align, port or absorb.

Builds the design-system artifact folder (build/design-system, ignored) from @catch/web-ui: the bundle the canvas mounts with React 18, web-ui's static Storybook, each card's guideline and Contract-story preview, fonts, the tokens pipeline's artifact tokens and a manifest of every file's and input's hash. --check rebuilds into a temporary folder and fails on a broken build, a missing guideline or system-name alias, a preview whose story is missing, a hash mismatch, or a stale build/design-system; --compare lists differences from another artifact folder. docs/design_system_publishing.md owns the loop.

Builds the exhaustive widget role, ownership, catalog, and consolidation classification from current Dart source, component contracts, and Widgetbook; explicit generation writes only an ignored build report.

Validates source-derived Widget ownership and identity across production roots. Shared Widgets must match reviewed ladder levels, role nouns, use-case comparisons, primary files and canonical names; new registry IDs cannot bypass collisions. No tracked inventory snapshot is trusted.
Validates stable visual-pattern family decisions, explicit member dispositions, constructor-qualified convergence targets, and required Widgetbook or source evidence.

rules.title: Consolidate UI through reviewed pattern families, not raw similarity pairs
rules.instruction: Generated similarity pairs and clusters are discovery evidence only. Assign candidates to a stable pattern family, render every available member side by side, choose the strongest visual/API reference, and record per-member canonical, repair, unify, register, or discard dispositions plus accepted visual deltas before creating a work order. Apply K/R/D rules only as post-decision implementation tactics, then rerender and prove the full family.

tools.description: Fails closed against a reachable base and transitively discovers widget subclasses across production roots. New or moved public widgets require Widgetbook coverage; shared widgets also require a canonical Catch* name and exact registry source identity. The generated markdown inventory is not an input. Private widgets and Widget-returning helpers remain blocked; generated exclusions are file-specific or suffix-specific.

rules.title: Keep widget catalog current when widget architecture changes
rules.instruction: Generate the inventory in docs/widget_catalog.md from production Widget declarations and design/components/catch.components.json; authored content is limited to Canonical Usage Decisions. Every new or moved public widget in shared, Consumer, or Host production source needs exact-name Widgetbook coverage. Shared Widgets require a canonical Catch* name and an exact source identity, reviewed ladder level and role in the registry; new or moved feature UI requires its feature-prefixed role name and canonical file suffix. The complete shared API must satisfy the naming grammar. Existing feature naming candidates remain source-derived review flags, not approved exceptions or a conformance claim. New or moved private widget classes and Widget-returning functions/getters are prohibited. Exact duplicate public widget class names and normalized public-name collisions fail unless every colliding symbol is an explicitly governed concept/member family. Regenerate affected inventory in the same pass when adding, deleting, moving, renaming, or materially changing a widget, primitive API, screen ownership model, sliver/tab structure, or reusable design-system role. Do not append release notes or per-change changelog headings.

tools.description: Finds oversized or duplicated Widgetbook variant matrices on demand from the logical repository snapshot without committing derived inventory.
Validates authored design decisions and P1 screen coverage; derives current gap and migration summaries without duplicated Markdown counts.
Reports every UI consolidation done-gate in design/components/consolidation_gates.json (tokens, component library, screens) against its zero target; never fails on the measured values.
Validates the exhaustive route-to-screen design parity coverage ledger.
Validates screen composition contracts against routes, captures, components, source paths, and Dart symbols.
Validates component contracts, primitive contract-state previews, and screen preview ids against generated Widgetbook directories.
Enforces role-derived Widgetbook evidence for concepts, members, contracted compositions, feature-owned compositions, and screen-owned widgets.

Serves the interactive Widgetbook comparison and canonical decision logging UI from current Widgetbook, classification, and on-demand source-derived similarity data, with pattern-family review first and dedupe evidence as a secondary queue.
Reports advisory raw Material controls and hand-rolled visual values in contracted screen implementation files.

Gates every Flutter Scaffold app bar, required pushed-route back affordance, raw navigation-bar implementation, shell-covering editor presentation, feature-owned header, and canonical top-bar action family against an exact reviewed screen-chrome role.

rules.title: Every screen declares one reviewed navigation-chrome owner
rules.instruction: Every handwritten Scaffold appBar must have an exact reviewed role in the screen-top-bar manifest: root or root-like screen voice uses CatchLegacyTopBar.screen, compact detail/edit/utility navigation uses CatchLegacyTopBar.route, and identity navigation uses CatchLegacyTopBar.identity; a screen framed by CatchScreen takes a CatchTopBar variant and needs no entry. Pushed routes that require an exit declare leading back and must configure an explicit back affordance. Raw Material or Cupertino navigation bars require an exact durable media-hero exception. Feature-owned Header and TopBar classes must be classified by symbol and owner, and full-screen editors that cover shell chrome must present through the root navigator. Broad file allowlists and unrelated canonical calls elsewhere in a file do not satisfy the contract.

tools.description: Reports advisory EdgeInsets inventory and likely hand-rolled screen gutter candidates across presentation and contracted screen implementation files.

rules.title: Screen gutters use semantic body and section ownership
rules.instruction: Screen, page, and body horizontal gutters should be owned by CatchInsets roles, CatchPageBody.screen, CatchSectionList.inset, CatchSection, CatchSectionList.sliver, or another documented layout primitive. Raw EdgeInsets rebuilt from CatchSpacing.screenPx/s5 in presentation code is a review candidate unless it is clearly component-local geometry.

tools.description: Enforces collapsed event create/edit disclosures and activity-palette accents on ActivityKind, EventInteractionModel, and PaceLevel Host choice fields.

rules.title: Prefer shared design primitives over repeated local shells
rules.instruction: Before creating local card, sheet, empty-state, rail, row, badge, skeleton, or section UI, check docs/widget_catalog.md and the existing Catch* primitives under packages/catch_ui/lib/src for an owner. Do not duplicate an existing primitive shell; extend the primitive or propose a variant through catalog review. Section titles have one owner: top-level groups route through CatchSection, contained card titles route through CatchSection.contained or a documented content primitive, and nested shared widgets must expose a content-only mode instead of repeating the parent section title. Underline tab/scope rails route through CatchPageTabBar or CatchChoiceInput.segmented; production code must not compose CatchChoiceButton directly because that forks divider, indicator, ink, and trailing-action alignment behavior.

tools.description: Reports raw Divider inventory, high-confidence CatchSection row-divider misuse, custom CatchField leading content without declared text-lane geometry, feature row groups that assign sibling divider flags, and thin feature-local CatchSection wrappers so row and section hairlines route through canonical roles.

Reports duplicate CatchSection titles, standalone header-plus-section shells, parallel label-plus-child kicker shells, and feature-local titled section/card shells so section header ownership routes through CatchSection or an explicit content primitive.
Reports rail callers that manually zero divider/header/list chrome instead of using embedded defaults or fullBleed opt-in.

Reports production direct CatchChoiceButton usage so underline tabs route through CatchChoiceInput.segmented or CatchPageTabBar rather than forking divider, indicator, ink, and trailing alignment behavior.
Validates exported design reference PNG metadata and supports advisory pixel comparison against UI capture artifacts.
Exports a single Claude Design data-screen-label panel to a reference PNG with explicit --write approval, optional fixed clip, and optional localStorage state.
Regenerates onboarding step reference PNGs from the local Claude handoff and validates generated output dimensions without launching Chrome.
Runs explicit source design invariants; identical registered scanner commands execute once in the shared tool runner. Snapshot handoff checks and advisory reports are separate explicit CLI options.
Checks every literal checkRateLimit action under functions/src has a matching RATE_LIMITS entry.

rules.title: Every checkRateLimit call passes its own required limit; the shared module holds no per-action table
rules.instruction: Declare each callable's limit where it calls checkRateLimit, inline or as a constant in a module only that callable family imports. The limit parameter is required, so no call falls back to a loose default. Never add a per-action limit table to functions/src/shared/rateLimit.ts: nearly every Function imports it, so editing it makes the backend deploy select every Function. Its frozen LEGACY_RATE_LIMITS table covers only callers whose module another task's claim holds; it may only shrink. demoOps and other privileged fan-out callables must declare dedicated limits.

tools.description: Keeps organizers canonical across contracts, Flutter, React, Functions, routes, media, and product copy while club remains a subtype. Flutter Dart file names, identifiers and localization keys must say organizer: what tool/architecture/rename_to_organizer.mjs would still rename fails, apart from the club subtype and names the generated schema contracts declare. Contract names, TypeScript identifiers and file names must say organizer too: what tool/architecture/rename_wire_to_organizer.mjs would still rename fails, apart from the club subtype and BigQuery columns.

rules.title: Organizer is the canonical entity and club is a subtype
rules.instruction: Use organizers, organizerId, organizer relationships, organizer callables, organizer media paths, and organizer product copy as the canonical authority. Club is allowed as organizerType club, real-world content, or an explicitly documented released-client compatibility projection only.

tools.description: Keeps contracts/catalogs/markets.json the one source of countries and cities: validates it against contracts/shared/market_catalog.schema.json and its cross-record lifecycle rules, fails when a generated copy (Functions, kernel Dart, admin launch markets, the Firestore rules launch-market block) is stale, and fails when tracked source names three or more catalog cities outside the shrink-only market_list_allowlist.json.

Runs on every change: fails when a generated market-catalog copy is stale, when the catalog breaks a cross-record lifecycle rule, or when tracked source names three or more catalog cities outside the shrink-only tool/contracts/market_list_allowlist.json. Needs no installed packages; contracts:market-catalog adds JSON Schema validation whenever the catalog changes.
Diffs current functions/README.md inventory rows and functions/src/index.ts exports in both directions while ratcheting existing omissions.

rules.instruction: The canonical functions/README.md function inventory must stay in sync with the actual exports in src/index.ts. Add a CI check that diffs the documented inventory against exports.

tools.description: Shrink-only Knip ratchet over unused files, exports, types and dependencies, and imports of undeclared packages. The Admin and Marketing lanes check their app plus packages/web-ui and packages/web-config on every change. This entry checks every JavaScript workspace except Functions when the Knip config, baseline or ratchet changes, and in full Tools runs (root package changes, nightly). Root tool/ and operations/ files are Knip entry points, so they can only add undeclared or broken imports and duplicate exports; full runs catch those. Functions joins once its lane runs the check.

Extracts structural fingerprints for explicit Dart widget files or an explicit disposable classification input for dedupe and similarity analysis.
Validates the cross-React primitive adoption tracker, classifies every exact-name website/admin primitive overlap, and rejects untracked @catch/web-ui exports.
Requires a unit test that imports each React feature controller/mutation hook, found from the source, without gating on aggregate coverage percentages.

rules.title: React controller coverage uses explicit behavior-test targets
rules.instruction: Every React feature controller or mutation hook needs a unit test that imports it and registers a test, normally beside it. Keep aggregate percentage reports informational.

tools.description: Keeps admin feature route/workspace entries and private panel modules below reviewed line ceilings after the large-screen decomposition pass.

rules.instruction: Keep route/workspace entries below 900 lines and feature-private panel modules below 1200 lines. Split by cohesive workflow before raising a ceiling; do not bypass the admin feature-export boundary with reusable-looking feature exports.

Proves the admin callable validator generator covers every adminApi callable and keeps every schema rule through compaction. Its output is built on demand by the Admin npm lifecycle and never tracked.

rules.instruction: Every callable used by adminApi must have a generated top-level validator; schema-backed requests validate on every live call and schema-backed responses validate in development or when VITE_ADMIN_VALIDATE_RESPONSES is enabled. pretypecheck regenerates the validators from their sources, so they cannot be stale.

tools.description: Binds declared cross-stack component symbols and enforces every public shared Widget constructor against the binding boolean, slot, callback, builder and enum-axis grammar using the syntax-only Dart collector.

rules.title: Cross-stack design-system implementations map to one checked component lexicon
rules.instruction: Every declared component surface symbol must exist in its implementation owner. Surface registry entries marked lexicon=true must reference a real catch.components id and exactly match that contract's surface symbol. Adopted cross-stack form primitives must declare a valid Flutter-owned interaction mode, while each stack retains its native implementation.

tools.description: Runs CI's Admin lane locally, reading its steps from the React surface workflow. Its checks here cover only the step reader; the steps themselves run in the Admin lane.
Builds the admin production surface, then ratchets the generated Vite-manifest JavaScript entry and largest async chunk.

rules.title: Admin route boundaries preserve production bundle budgets
rules.instruction: Keep data/query controllers behind lazy route boundaries and fail the production build when the JavaScript entry or largest async chunk exceeds the reviewed byte budget.

tools.description: Ratchets Catch-authored admin Storybook route and feature chunks while excluding framework and accessibility-vendor runtime chunks.

rules.title: Admin Storybook preserves app-authored feature chunk boundaries
rules.instruction: Keep Catch-authored admin feature and route-story chunks within the reviewed Storybook budgets. Split feature code and large generated datasets with named Rollup boundaries; do not hide regressions by raising the general Vite warning limit.

rules.title: Registry-ready React stories have deterministic visual baselines
rules.instruction: Every Storybook registry entry marked ready must resolve to a built story that renders with reduced motion and loaded fonts; a story that cannot render fails. Each desktop and mobile capture is compared with committed baselines for the current operating system at the configured pixel tolerance, and CI reports changed, missing or stale baselines in the job summary and diagnostics artifact without failing while the product is still changing visually. Never compare Darwin-authored system-ui pixels against Linux; CI uses reviewed Ubuntu 24.04 baselines.

tools.description: Runs durable business workflows with shadow-safe defaults and stable JSON output.
Invokes catalogued admin callables with strict requests, dry-run mutation defaults, exact action/target confirmations, App Check, and local plus remote hash-only receipts.
Keeps every admin API callable aligned with one strict catalog action, Functions export, workflow membership, role set, schema-valid example, and explicit mutation confirmation policy.

Generates the typed admin-browser and Functions action-catalog views from contracts/admin/actions/ on demand through the Admin and Functions npm lifecycles. --validate checks the catalog's own links; the views are never tracked.

Validates a Supply Intake admin export locally by default and, only with explicit apply, alias-bound environment/project, production, and run confirmation flags, imports or repairs the immutable shadow projection in server-owned Firestore collections.

Reads one explicit environment, project, event, organizer, channel, sender and purpose through the production setup readers, then prints a schema-validated, credential-free runtime, sender and budget review that grants no dispatch authority.

rules.title: Durable business workflows stay outside repository tooling
rules.instruction: Resumable runs, work items, leases, budgets, decisions, receipts, and learning state belong in operations/. Legacy tool folders remain compatibility producers. Every workflow manifest stays bound to its executable commands, ordered states, sources, capabilities, and capacity. Ordinary admin actions share one catalog across GUI and CLI; strict schemas, role-gated callables, dry-run mutation defaults, confirmations, and hash-only receipts must not drift. Shadow mode fails closed. The admin projection crosses into Firestore only through the dry-run-first trusted importer, and publication requires separately authorized execution.

tools.description: Keeps durable business workflows under operations/ by scanning every tool code root for runtime imports or orchestration markers, while ratcheting known legacy artifact producers.
Binds each durable workflow manifest to its live CLI commands, ordered stage and lifecycle contracts, source profiles, disabled capabilities, and platform capacity.
Runs fingerprint extractor regression tests for seeded widget dedupe fixtures and state-class folding.

Checks the live static Riverpod provider, consumer, override, family, alias, and Mutation graph while requiring a current // provider-graph: review next to each questionable relationship; deterministic JSON is emitted only on demand.

rules.title: Use feature-owned provider seams
rules.instruction: If a feature has a view model, controller, or feature-specific provider, screens should use that seam rather than reaching around it to a lower-level repository provider. Use generated overridable repository factories for dependency injection and generated Notifier/AsyncNotifier/StreamNotifier owners according to synchronous, loaded or streaming state responsibility. A generated wrapper around a business ChangeNotifier does not make its state lifecycle declarative. Pure imperative service helpers, local Flutter mechanics and named framework bridges remain valid. The AST graph requires exact path/symbol/operation reviews with bounded callsites; planned debt and watch signals are not compliance, and new owners or replacement operations cannot inherit a file/count exception. Its parsed-source limits still require manual lifecycle and domain-fence review.

rules.title: Keep the static Riverpod topology current and reviewed
rules.instruction: Derive and check the complete live Riverpod source graph from Dart ASTs. Keep providers, families, consumers, aliases, overrides, and Mutations resolvable; reject duplicate or dangling providers, provider-internal unresolved refs, reactive cycles, unreviewed architecture candidates, and stale review decisions. Do not commit generated graph views; emit deterministic JSON or summary evidence only on demand. Core-owned providers must not orchestrate feature data, and provider aliases should be removed when the canonical owner can be used directly.

rules.title: A read owner declares one lifetime
rules.instruction: A provider that reaches .snapshots(), a Firestore .get(), httpsCallable or callHostCrm declares exactly one lifetime in its build, and is keepAlive: true only with an account-free // keepalive: decision. Contract: docs/screen_data_caching.md.

rules.title: A lifetime takes a CachePolicies member
rules.instruction: Pass only a CachePolicies member to a lifetime, and never build a CachePolicy outside that table. Contract: docs/screen_data_caching.md.

rules.title: Cached account data is keyed by session
rules.instruction: A timed or session read owner of account data holds an AuthenticatedSession in its key. Contract: docs/screen_data_caching.md.

rules.title: No raw DateTime in a cached key
rules.instruction: Time enters a timed or session read owner's key only as a CacheTimeBucket, never as a raw DateTime. Contract: docs/screen_data_caching.md.

rules.title: Presentation invalidates read owners only to retry
rules.instruction: Presentation code invalidates or refreshes a read owner only in a retry or pull-to-refresh, and a retry targets the read owner rather than a composition. Contract: docs/screen_data_caching.md.

rules.title: Listeners take no write invalidation or tags
rules.instruction: A write does not invalidate a Firestore listener provider, and a listener declares no cache tags, because it delivers its own updates. Contract: docs/screen_data_caching.md.

rules.title: A kept-alive handwritten provider says why
rules.instruction: A handwritten provider without .autoDispose carries a // keepalive: marker. Contract: docs/screen_data_caching.md.

tools.description: Checks and idempotently provisions the Firebase Storage service-agent role required for Storage rules to read Firestore.

rules.title: Storage rules cross-service dependencies stay provisioned and live-probed
rules.instruction: Storage rules that call firestore.get or firestore.exists require roles/firebaserules.firestoreServiceAgent on every environment's Firebase Storage service agent. Storage deploys must fail their IAM preflight when it is absent, and authenticated upload/delete behavior must remain live-probeable without weakening participant rules.

tools.description: Runs an authenticated chat-image upload/delete canary through deployed Storage rules and removes its bounded fixture.

Signs in as a synthetic Host that manages a synthetic organizer and runs the Host app's rules-checked Firestore reads and read callables against one deployed environment. Dry-run by default; production runs Firestore reads only unless --allow-prod-callables.
Validates the live CatchField facade and section contracts deterministically; an explicit non-check run writes an ignored build report rather than tracked governance evidence.
Rejects hand-rolled device-bottom padding in product code so scroll owners use the shell-aware terminal-clearance primitives.

Registers every consumer and host StatefulShellBranch, verifies adaptive shell adoption, rejects superseded root APIs, and rejects raw empty/error sliver composition. Analyzer-backed UI composition contracts separately own route layout roles and terminal geometry.

rules.title: Root screens declare semantic composition and clear adaptive shell chrome
rules.instruction: Every direct consumer and host StatefulShellBranch must be registered in tool/design/root_screen_composition_contracts.json. Exact route-to-layout ownership belongs in design/screens/catch.screens.json and is enforced by the analyzer-backed UI composition gate. Ordinary roots select CatchRootScreenScaffold.standard, .sections, or .fullBleed, or the matching CatchRootScreenScrollView constructor. Section roots use .sections for full-width rows with the canonical title-to-body rhythm. Roots with pinned peer navigation use .withPrimaryRail plus one of CatchRootScreenPageScrollView.standard, .fullBleed, or .embeddedViewport. These semantic constructors centralize SafeArea(bottom: false), title-to-body rhythm, gutters, responsive content width, field obstruction, refresh, and terminal clearance. Box-layout terminal empty/error branches use CatchStateViewport; presentation slivers use CatchStateViewport.sliver, CatchSliverEmptyState, or CatchSliverErrorState rather than composing SliverFillRemaining directly, so the same shell obstruction controls their optical center.

tools.description: Enforces manifest-backed root ownership, retired duplicate-impact-authority absence, Git expectations, protected cleanup boundaries, audit policies, and portable Markdown links. Every *_baseline.json names its owning document and a target-zero phase heading.

rules.title: Repository-root entries have explicit owners and safe cleanup contracts
rules.instruction: Every root entry must match exactly one manifest classification. Cleanup is dry-run first and mutates only an explicit allowlisted scope; tracked files, protected paths, worktrees, symlinks, path escapes, and machine-local Markdown links are rejected.

tools.description: Keeps the brand in packages/brand/brand.json: fails when its domain, Instagram handle, support email or phone is hard-coded outside the record, its generated copies and managed surfaces, or the display name appears in website copy; the allowlist of unmigrated files may only shrink. Also fails when a generated copy or managed surface is stale.
Reports regenerable repository state and deletes only manifest-allowlisted paths after explicit apply and scope flags.
Requires an explicit Firebase environment for Functions deploy and log commands.
Rejects removed generic row and collection skeleton recipes in app source and screen-local root title typography overrides.
Internal synthetic RSVP fixture builder dispatched and checked by the active demo:rsvp-preview owner.
Builds an isolated synthetic RSVP form and review fixture; does not initialize Firebase or send messages.
Renders production Host widgets with localhost synthetic repository adapters.
Serves the production public form renderer with synthetic in-memory submission adapters.
Runs normal roster import and CRM projection against an isolated synthetic store; never initializes Firebase Admin.
Renders the production spreadsheet parser and mapping sheet for a local synthetic XLSX fixture.
Checks or explicitly provisions the dedicated form upload runtime identity; default is read-only and production apply is separately gated.
Compares exact Git base/head selector snapshots and requires conservative full validation for control edits; checks actual CI plan and fanout against the same-source obligations.
Reuses exact-main Marketing and capture execution only with matching workflow, repository, source and attempt identity; offline fixtures reject missing, failed or cancelled evidence.

Decides when a source CI run passes the website release gate: the whole run succeeded, or (sprint floor, owner decision 11 Nov 2026) its Required CI job succeeded and only the reporting-only lanes failed. Pins the reporting lanes to ci.yml's Required CI.
Source guard imported by design:component-contracts; rejects generic operational card and local empty-state anatomy on migrated Host surfaces.

Materializes the two exact-source route/catalog inventories while preserving authored guidance and coverage decisions. Offline real-Git checks use Node and Git; no Flutter or network. CI writes an ignored source/run-bound two-output receipt; later checks verify current inventory bytes before reusing exact drift commands.

Imports exact-id/source/run/attempt/digest-bound canonical captures and verifies website dist bytes. Offline checks use Node, Git and Python 3 standard-library ZIP support; synthetic renderer commands do not invoke Flutter or providers. The real import additionally requires gh and read-only Actions access.
Validates the shared icon-role catalog against the vendored Flutter font, locked React family version and activity kinds, and verifies the generated Flutter CatchIcons and @catch/web-ui role maps.

rules.title: Features draw catalogued icon roles through the shared icon layer
rules.instruction: Features name semantic icon roles from the shared catalog. Keep the vendored Flutter font and React icon family at the catalogued version, with exactly one role per activity kind. Existing direct family references and legacy CatchIcons aliases may only decrease; record each reduction rather than increasing an allowance. The catalog owns glyph selection, so changing a family does not require feature code to select glyphs.

tools.description: Vendors the icon family's Flutter font and codepoints from its static npm package at the version package-lock.json resolves for the React package, pins the version and font hash in the icon-role catalog, and regenerates both icon layers; run it on a lucide-react bump so design:icon-catalog passes.
Ratchets Flutter and React icon-family bypasses and legacy CatchIcons aliases downward; rejects growth and unrecorded reductions.
